column1: # Issue 1372: the ONE parity table for the dantesync clock-discipline classifier and the date-master
# verdict. BOTH implementations read it: the bash `clock_discipline_class` /
# sourced by scripts/clock-offset-guard.sh) and the python twin `classify_clock_discipline` /
# tests/python/test_clock_discipline_1372.py. The journal_grade column pins the JOURNAL path's date
# Columns (TAB-separated): case, status, class, date_verdict (margin 1000 us, micro bound 5 ms,
# daily bound 3000 ms, now = DANTESYNC_DATE_NOW_S 1790501400 = 2026-09-27T09:30:00Z), unlocked,
#   status  = `@<repo-relative path>` to a /status JSON file, or an inline compact JSON object.
#   date_verdict = none (not the date master) | ok | out | paused (a dantesync 1.11.0 master whose
#              micro-corrections are paused: no UTC reading) | unknown (master, fields unreadable)
#   unlocked = yes only for clock_discipline=ptp_phase_lock with ptp_phase_locked=false (the
#              named PTP-PHASE UNLOCKED failure: clock_discipline_unlocked), else no
#   journal_grade = how a date-authority journal line `(..., step bound 50000us)` is graded when the
#              SAME node's /status is this row (margin 1000 us, micro bound 5 ms):
#              micro:<us> (a micro-capable 1.11.x date master: median-only on micro bound + margin)
#              | step:<us> (a readable /status that is not one: the journal's step bound + margin)
#              | step-unread:<us> (no readable /status, no date_authority: the step bound, named)
#              | unknown (a micro-capable master whose flags are not JSON booleans)
# The four @ files are /status captured read-only from the live fleet on 26.9.2026 (strih-lx master
# and the stream slave, both dantesync 1.9.0) plus two legacy nodes synthesized from the pre-1.9.0
# field shape (no clock_discipline / ptp_phase_locked / date_* fields).
# The two 1.11.1 @ files are /status captured read-only from the same two live nodes on 26.9.2026
# after the fleet roll to dantesync 1.11.1 (dantesync PR 121 date micro-corrections + PR 122): the
# master reads date_offset_error_ms=0.471 with last_date_step_kind=micro; the slave is a follower.
# They replaced the synthesized 1.11.0 fixtures. A master that carries
# date_correction_falling_behind is graded on the micro bound (DANTESYNC_DATE_MICRO_BOUND_MS,
# default 5) + margin, falling behind = out, paused = paused; a master without it (1.9.0 / 1.10.0)
# is graded on date_step_bound_ms exactly as before (the mixed fleet during the roll).
# dantesync 1.12.0 (PR 123, the NIGHTLY date step): a master whose date_correction_mode is "daily"
# corrects nothing by day -- its date_offset_error_ms grows to a day's drift (~1.5 s on the rig) until
# ONE coordinated step at the nightly window (02:00 UTC). It is graded on its schedule: the next
# window (date_daily_next_utc) within (now, now + 24 h 30 min], the last nightly step
# (date_daily_last_step_ts) within the last 26 h (null = none seen since the master started, a NOTE;
# up to 30 min in the future = announced, not landed yet), and |error| <= DANTESYNC_DATE_DAILY_BOUND_MS
# (default 3000) + margin. A read, wrong field wins over an unreadable one (out before unknown).
# journal_grade: daily:<us> (a live schedule: the journal median on the daily bound + margin) |
# daily-out (a missing / past / far schedule, or a stale last step) | daily-unknown (a schedule
# field, the mode or the daily bound unreadable). date_correction_mode "micro" or "" keeps the
# 1.11 grade. The two 1.12.0 @ files are SYNTHESIZED from the 1.11.1 captures plus the four new
# fields in dantesync src/status.rs order, until a live capture after the roll replaces them.
